modelAnswer: An exothermic reaction evolves heat and transfers energy from the chemical system to its surroundings. An endothermic reaction absorbs heat and transfers energy from the surroundings to the system.

modelAnswer: An exothermic reaction releases heat to the surroundings, so its enthalpy change is negative. Combustion of a fuel is an example. For example, methane combustion releases heat: $\mathrm{CH}_{4}+2\mathrm{O}_{2}\rightarrow\mathrm{CO}_{2}+2\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}$.
stem: What are exothermic reactions? Give an example of an exothermic chemical reaction.

modelAnswer: An endothermic reaction absorbs heat from the surroundings, so its enthalpy change is positive. An example is photosynthesis, which requires energy. An exothermic reaction releases heat and has negative $\Delta H$, whereas an endothermic reaction absorbs heat and has positive $\Delta H$.
stem: What are endothermic reactions? Give an example of an endothermic chemical reaction.

modelAnswer: Exothermic reactions transfer heat to the surroundings and have negative $\Delta H$; combustion and respiration are examples. Endothermic reactions absorb heat from the surroundings and have positive $\Delta H$; photosynthesis is an example. Breaking bonds absorbs energy, while forming bonds releases energy.

modelAnswer: On an energy profile, plot reaction progress horizontally and energy vertically. For an exothermic reaction, products lie below reactants and $\Delta H<0$; for an endothermic reaction, products lie above reactants and $\Delta H>0$. Each curve rises from reactants to a peak; the vertical rise to the peak is activation energy. A catalyzed curve has a lower peak but the same reactant and product energies.

modelAnswer: Activation energy is the minimum extra energy that colliding particles must have for an effective collision. On a pathway diagram, it is the energy difference between the reactants and the peak. For catalyzed and uncatalyzed pathways, the catalyst lowers the peak and therefore lowers activation energy, but it does not change the overall enthalpy change.
